title: Machine learning identifies a synthesis-time relationship in oxygen-reduction catalysts
summary: Learned models ranked factors in 225 literature-derived catalyst records and highlighted pyrolysis duration alongside temperature. Researchers then varied these conditions in iron-nitrogen-carbon catalysts and measured a volcano-like relationship between duration and oxygen-reduction half-wave potential, alongside changes in nitrogen species. This is a laboratory synthesis-performance relationship, not proof that model importance alone establishes an atomic mechanism or that the result generalizes to other catalyst families.
ai_technology: Supervised tree ensembles; artificial neural networks; SHAP feature interpretation

evidence.tested: Model-guided control experiments varied pyrolysis duration and temperature in ZIF-derived Fe-N-C catalysts, with electrochemical measurements and nitrogen-species characterization.
evidence.unknown: Feature importance is associative; the represented relationship does not establish every proposed atomic mechanism. Independent replication, other catalyst families and practical fuel-cell benefits remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Nine learned model families, including tree ensembles and neural networks, related catalyst properties and synthesis parameters to activity and pyridinic-nitrogen content; model interpretation prioritized duration for controlled experiments.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher front metadata and abstract; complete official supplementary modeling, synthesis and characterization sections, including model-importance tables and control-series captions. Main article body was paywalled and not read. Current Crossref update relationships checked.
